newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybean futures end lower on mad cow rumor.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybean futures end lower on mad cow rumor.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower on Wednesday, led by a slide in corn futures on wire service reports that a Indiana rose grower may have died from Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, the human counterpart to mad cow disease, traders said.
"That's what cracked the cattle and it's cracking the grains, too," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
The Indiana Health Department said it could not confirm press reports that the death of the 62-year-old man was from CJD but said the state has several cases of CJD annually.
The disease has been called the human version of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), the "madcow" cattle disease that caused a consumer panic in Europe in the past year.
Traders said a scare in the beef industry could limit consumer beef purchases and lessen demand for livestock feed.
Soybeans ended 11-1/4 to 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower with May down 3-3/4 at $8.32-1/4.
Losses in nearbys were curbed by calls for a national port strike in Brazil that may hamper soy exports, traders said.

A union official on Wednesday said Brazilian stevedores will go on national strike in sympathy with their colleagues at Santos port at 0500 CDT Thursday (1000 GMT) for 48 hours. Union sources earlier said the strike would begin at 2200 CDT.
